messages:
andrea: Heads-up — nightly perf dashboard showed a steady widening in p50->p99 latency after the merge-rollforward last night. p99 up ~12% on g4 pool. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/perf/nightly?run=174998

kai: saw that too. Is this across all kernels or only last-gen kernels?

maria: graph shows the spike aligns exactly with commit 202b3f7 (kernel-selector + batching tweak). Could be kernel scoring or batching window change.

sre-bot: CI job perf-nightly/runner-42 failed 3/10 perf checks. Job: https://ci.redwood/internal/job/420/perf — details attached in job artifacts.

lucas: can we get a flamegraph or a sampled profile? thinking KV thrash or more kernel hops.

andrea: uploaded a tiny flame snippet from the profiler (brief):
```text
p99 path: kernel_choose() -> select_score() -> batch_coalesce()
hot functions: kv_cache_lookup (12%), kernel_dispatch (46%), serial_merge (9%)
```

kai: interesting — serial_merge climbed. that points at batch coalescing heuristics changing behavior. any batching-window changes in that rollforward?

maria: yes — the rollforward included a tweak: `BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS` lowered from 8 -> 4 to reduce median latency. suspect this increases fragmentation and kernel-churning.

anil: can you paste the PR/commit? i'll try a local reproduce + quick bisect.

andrea: commit 202b3f7 (PR #879). excerpt: 
```diff
- BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS = 8
+ BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS = 4
```

lucas: lowering wait means more small batches => more kernel selection decisions => less kernel reuse => more KV misses. kv_cache_lookup % increase matches that hypothesis.

kai: quick mitigation: pause rollouts and revert that flag on canary first. if canary improves we revert globally.

andrea: i've paused the canary rollout for the model-serving pool and created an incident: INC-3472. Pinged infra to halt global rollforward.

sre-bot: Incident INC-3472 created by andrea at 1749994360

maria: proposal: revert the batching change in master and re-run nightly. who will own the revert?

anil: i'll open a revert PR now, include perf test, ETA ~30m.

lucas: also filing PERF-882 to add a synthetic perf unit that stresses many small prompt sizes and counts kernel selector churn. will link from INC-3472.

kai: if revert confirms improvement we should add a guard to kernel selector: prefer_streaming only when batch_size > 2 (avoid streaming preference on heavily fragmented batches).

andrea: noted. @oncall please watch p95/p99 for the next two runs and escalate if >5% regress vs baseline.

oncall: got it. i'll monitor dashboards and post updates in this thread.

maria: CI perf job artifacts also show ~18% throughput drop on dedicated-GPU integration tests — so impact isn't isolated to latency.

andrea: thanks — capturing that in INC-3472. we'll keep this thread for triage notes and link PRs. thanks everyone for quick responses :thumbsup:
